intro: If you're in Prachinburi town for work or a road trip and want a freshly opened stay with clean rooms, a warm feel and a café right on-site — Jiphome Prachin Buri is a name the local-travel crowd keeps mentioning. It's a 3-star café-stay in Rop Mueang, Mueang district, opened in 2025. The draw is a roughly 25 sqm King room that real guests praise for being clean, fresh-smelling and spacious, plus the in-house Jiphome Cafe so a good morning coffee is steps away. Rooms start from about ฿630/night, climbing toward ฿900 on holidays or late bookings.

body.html: The heart of Jiphome is that it feels more like staying at a friend's home than checking into a hotel. It opened in 2025 in Rop Mueang, Mueang Prachinburi, with warm, easygoing decor and an in-house Jiphome Cafe. Past guests agree that walking in just feels comfortable rather than like a standard hotel check-in — a good fit if you want a soft, relaxed setting to unwind after a day on the road.

The main room type is a King room of about 25 sqm with an added sofa bed. Each room has AC, a TV and free Wi-Fi. What real reviews consistently praise is how clean the rooms are, the fresh scent, and how roomy they feel for a price in the few-hundred to low-thousand baht range. The sofa bed means three people can sleep comfortably, which works for a couple travelling with a child or a small group of friends.
"Clean, fresh-smelling, spacious, with a warm homey feel. Lovely owner and a café on-site too — great value for the price."

Facilities are right-sized for a small stay like this. There's on-site parking, the in-house Jiphome cafe and restaurant serving local dishes and coffee, a convenience store and a multipurpose room. Mornings, you can sip coffee in the property's own café without heading out. Another point many travellers look for: it is pet-friendly (dogs and cats, with a surcharge of around ฿250), which is hard to find among Prachinburi town stays.

The in-town location makes onward trips easy. It's a short drive to Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital and its Thai traditional-medicine museum, a provincial landmark. From here you can push on to the Noen Hom area at the foot of Khao Yai, or toward Kabin Buri. Using Jiphome as a one-night base in town before exploring further works out neatly.

A few honest things to know before booking. This is a small, newly opened stay, so there are still only a handful of real reviews — the scores reflect the first wave of guests, and some service touches may still be settling in. Some rooms have no fridge/minibar, so ask first if you need to chill food or medicine. There's also a review noting the key-card slot sits low so you have to crouch to tap it — minor, but worth knowing. And being an in-town stay, there's no pool or spa like a resort.

Overall, Jiphome is a newly opened café-stay earning praise for cleanliness and a warm atmosphere at a friendly price. Rooms start around ฿630 for the King, rising to roughly ฿900 on holidays or late bookings. If you want an in-town stay with clean rooms, an on-site café, the option to bring your dog or cat, and you're not chasing fancy facilities, it's a worthwhile pick for a night in Prachinburi.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you're here to relax, make the most of the in-house Jiphome cafe — order a coffee or green tea and ease into the morning. If you're bringing a pet, flag it and confirm the surcharge at booking. And since it's a small property with limited rooms, book ahead on long weekends as it fills up fast.
